note: PRESERVATION property. The pre-fix watchdog already never managed services - its own header promised it - so this test cannot fail against 139726e without contriving a failure, and a contrived non-zero baseline is precisely the false evidence condition 8 exists to police. The passing capture below proves the property PRE-EXISTED the fix; the mutation captures prove the test can actually detect its loss.
kind_derivation: exit_code == 0 => preservation (product ruling, 2026-08-22). Declared here only because it AGREES with the capture; a disagreement is a hard FAIL.

production.symbol: the alert path's read-only service diagnostics, and the alive-path early return
production.symbol_note: A flat bash script has no function symbols on these paths, so the binding is made exact by the committed patches rather than by a name: each names the surrounding lines and applies cleanly to this file at bdcdcfc.

mutations.target_path: alert path (reached when the Program is NOT alive)
mutations.mutation: insert `systemctl --user restart omnigent-server` before the read-only is-active diagnostics
mutations.rationale: the realistic regression: a well-meaning 'the service looks dead, restart it' self-heal. Restarting kills in-flight worker turns.
mutations.subtests_passed_reason: the alive branch returns before this block, so M1 is unreachable there. Covered by M2.

mutations.target_path: alive path (early return when the Program IS alive)
mutations.mutation: insert `systemctl --user restart omnigent-host` into the alive branch before its exit 0
mutations.rationale: M1 cannot reach the alive branch, so without M2 the path='alive' subtest would have no mutation proof at all - the same self-attestation trap this whole record exists to avoid.

mutation_hygiene: Both patches are EVIDENCE only. They are generated, applied to a scratch working tree, captured, and reverted; `git diff -- deploy/nightshift-watchdog.sh` is empty in the commit that adds them. The mutated code is never committed to a mergeable branch. Re-captured after the issue-#26 naming edit to deploy/nightshift-watchdog.sh; both patches still `git apply --check` clean (git tolerates line offsets) and both still exit 1. applied_to_sha is refreshed to the commit carrying that edit.
insufficient_alternative: test_rt11_the_instrumented_boundary_can_actually_fire is retained and is NOT this evidence: it appends a mutation string to the journal by hand, so it proves the DETECTOR parses such a call, not that one reached from the watchdog's real code path would arrive at the boundary. Only M1/M2 prove that.
perishability_note: Raised as finding N2 on PR #25: condition 8 as drafted requires the mutant patch to apply to THE TIP, so this evidence perishes if any CONTEXT line changes - verified that rewording a nearby comment is sufficient to break it. Recommended remedy there is a `mutant_base_sha` field mirroring `baseline_sha`. Until that is settled these captures are re-run whenever this file changes.
